set_text.text: Safety stock is the extra stock you hold for days that do not go to plan. A busier day or a late truck draws on it. It is sized from how much demand and lead time swing, not from the averages alone. Here that comes to 229 cases.
How far demand and lead time stray from their averages. Two lines that both sell 120 cases a day can need very different buffers.
Supplier shorts. A truck that arrives late is in the formula, but one that arrives with part of the order is not. A partial delivery eats the buffer without warning.
A swing with names on it
For a distributor, the 35 case swing can trace back to a few accounts that order big and irregularly. Part of the buffer is paying for their pattern.
Who uses a safety stock calculator
It is built for independent food distributors who hold dated and dry lines in their own warehouse. Anyone who decides how much spare stock to keep, or defends that call in cash, should run it.
